alana (support): FYI customer ACME flagged a sudden embeddings bill spike and says the dashboard shows 'vectors' but numbers look like token counts. asking for urgent help.
kevin (eng-analytics): Can you paste the customer dashboard URL + account id? Also any example request ids?
alana (support): https://console.redwood.ai/account/ACME/usage -> they linked the 'Embeddings usage' chart. Account: acme-corp-42. Example request_id from their support logs: req_01Gz9XJ7A6Z1
priya (product): did they say when this started? could be the new batching change we shipped last week.
alana (support): They reported starting yesterday ~16:20 UTC. Chart shows a big jump at that time. Billing saw ~3x units for embeddings.
mike (sre): @kevin can you check ingestion/ETL around 16:20? maybe duplicate events
kevin (eng-analytics): Looking at ingestion logs for acme-corp-42. I see events with event_type: "embedding.request" and separate events with event_type: "embedding.item" for each vector. Our aggregator currently sums both.
kevin (eng-analytics): quick proof: grep on request_id in usage-raw:

```
$ jq -c 'select(.request_id=="req_01Gz9XJ7A6Z1")' /data/usage-raw/2026-06-12/*.json
{"event_type":"embedding.request","request_id":"req_01Gz9XJ7A6Z1","tokens":128,"vectors":1}
{"event_type":"embedding.item","request_id":"req_01Gz9XJ7A6Z1","item_index":0,"vectors":1}
```

kevin (eng-analytics): The offline job usage-aggregator was summing tokens from both event kinds. So if a batched request had n items, it counted the request-level units and all n item-level units -> double/overcount.
sanjay (eng-platform): That matches the customer repro: they used batch size 4, so numbers look ~4x. The chart label says 'vectors' but backend units were a mix of 'vectors' and token-units. UI mapping is wrong.
priya (product): Ugh. So two problems: (1) aggregator shouldn't sum both kinds, (2) UI label unit mapping is inconsistent. We need immediate mitigation and a long-term fix.
kevin (eng-analytics): Short term: I can patch the aggregator to only count event_type:embedding.item (and ignore embedding.request) for embeddings usage, and re-run the last 24h job to correct counts. Longer term: dedupe by (request_id,item_index) and normalize event types.
kevin (eng-analytics): Proposed aggregator diff (pseudocode):

```
# before: sum all events where metric == 'embeddings'
for ev in events:
  total += ev.units

# after: prefer item-level events, fallback to request-level if no items
by_req = group_by(events, ev.request_id)
for rid, evs in by_req.items():
  items = [e for e in evs if e.event_type=='embedding.item']
  if items:
    total += sum(i.vectors for i in items)
  else:
    req = find(evs, lambda e: e.event_type=='embedding.request')
    if req: total += req.vectors
```

alana (support): Customer asked for a timeline and credits. Any ETA to re-run and fix the chart?
kevin (eng-analytics): I can deploy a hotfix to the aggregator config in ~1h (low-risk) and re-run backfill for acme-corp-42 for 24-48 hours. Backfill will take ~30-45m.
sanjay (eng-platform): I'll review and approve if it's just changing the filter + dedupe. Also need to add a migration so future pipelines don't reintroduce both event types.
priya (product): For UI: hide the 'units' suffix and change tooltip to "vectors (deduped)" until counts are validated. I'll put up a tiny patch.
mike (sre): Ops note: re-running backfill will spike compute. I'll open a brief maintenance window to avoid autoscaler surprises.
kevin (eng-analytics): I also found older events where request-level vectors were 0 and items included counts; aggregator logic assumed request-level present. We'll need to normalize ingestion to always emit only one canonical event per item.
priya (product): Action list:
- kevin: deploy aggregator filter + backfill (ETA 1.5h)
- sanjay: add dedupe migration and review (ETA today EOD)
- priya: UI label/tooltip patch (ETA 2h)
- mike: ops window + monitor (ETA now)
- alana: send ACME interim note: we'll investigate, provide timeline, offer provisional credit

alana (support): sending message now: "We're investigating and will have a fix and corrected metrics within ~2 hours. We'll issue a credit for the spike and follow up with root cause." :thumbsup:
kevin (eng-analytics): Patch pushed to canary. Aggregator now ignoring embedding.request when embedding.item present. Starting backfill for acme-corp-42.
ops-bot: Backfill job queued: job_id=bf-20260612-01, estimated_time=35m
kevin (eng-analytics): Backfill completed. Preliminary numbers show ACME usage reduced from ~3.2M vectors to ~0.8M vectors in the spike window (matches expected batch factor). I'm going to push corrected numbers to the dashboard cache now.
priya (product): updating ACME billing to issue a provisional credit for the delta. bookkeeping-ops handle the rest.
alana (support): customer notified and appreciated the quick turnaround. thank you team :heart:
kevin (eng-analytics): follow-up: we'll add a unit test to ensure aggregator doesn't double count. I'll open PR and tag eng-platform.
sanjay (eng-platform): noted. Also adding alert if embedding.request and embedding.item both appear for same request_id in future so we can catch ingestion anomalies earlier.
kevin (eng-analytics): TL;DR root cause: analytics pipeline summed both request-level and item-level embedding events leading to overcount for batched requests. Fix: prefer item-level events + backfill. UI label updated while we verify. Credits issued.
alana (support): closing loop with ACME and marking escalation resolved."
